column4: on (NVK_CHANNEL_RECOVER=0 in the settings file: a channel fault ends the device, as in 2.9)
column7: After a GPU fault on one channel NVK rebuilds that channel and the application carries on, instead of losing its device.

Test hook for the channel recovery: NVK_FAULT_INJECT=<mode>:<n>[:<process>] stalls or faults the n-th submission of a process once, so the rebuild can be watched. Set it in the settings file: a release plugin forgets it from the environment.
Keep CPU-written memory in system RAM: On by default for stability; off places it in video memory (faster in some games, unsafe for the desktop).
Built-in per-application profiles: On by default; off turns every shipped per-application profile off.
Card for an application: With more than one card: 0 is the primary, 1 the second and so on (up to 7), for every application (1) or per application (Game=1,*=0).

column4: on (NVMTL_DROP_REPORT=0 in the settings file: it is reported as completed, as in 2.9)
column7: A command buffer that was dropped while its channel was rebuilt is reported to the application as an error.
Frame-rate limit: One number for every application (60) or a list per application (Game=60,*=0). 10 to 1000; 0 is unlimited. Never applies to WindowServer.
Low-latency mode (GPU work queued ahead): How many parts of GPU work may be queued ahead, 1 to 32 (default 16). A low number cuts input lag and can cost frame rate.

column4: on (nvrmdma=0: no IOMMU mapper -> the 2.9 path; mapper present -> the GPU is not started)
column7: With an IOMMU (VT-d) translating for the GPU, the GPU is given the mapper's bus addresses instead of physical ones; without a mapper nothing changes. On a machine with a mapper nvrmdma=0 is not a way back to 2.9, whose untranslated addresses are wrong there: the GPU is left unstarted and the log says why.
